about: How the President's own record shapes the address (owner, Oct 27, 2026: 'it needs to flow like a real speech ... if there are 58 laws, there are 58 choices they have in the speech'). Any policy question in the bill catalog can be a priority: the President's recorded stance on each (`ownStance`) picks the few they lead with and the one line they will not cross, and the laws engine's answer in force for the question (the nation's for a federal question, the player's state's for any other) is what the address says about it. `numbersBySubject` says which of the country's numbers bear on a catalog subject, so a priority can be argued from one. It holds no sentence: the words are the opening-speech bank's.

mannerTraits.about: The recorded traits that make a President's address plain-spoken or polished: the manner is whichever side the President's traits sum higher on, polished when they tie.

prioritiesMax.note: The most priorities the address leads with, each a stake, a law and an ask (real inaugural addresses name two to four).

priorityStanceShare.note: A supported question is a priority while the President's stance on it is at least this share of their strongest stance; the address is as long as the President's convictions are many.

storyFigures.note: How many of the country's numbers the story of the country cites besides the nation's unemployment rate, always told under its scope: those that moved most over the year, apart from the ones the priorities argue from.
